title: The influence of an enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) nurse in accelerating mobility and recovery after colorectal surgery: A randomized controlled trial
summary: The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of dedicated perioperative care provided by an ERAS nurse on postoperative recovery following colorectal surgery. Specifically, the study will investigate the impact of ERAS nurse support on postoperative mobility, adherence to the ERAS protocol (ERAS compliance), and patient satisfaction.
conditions: Patients undergoing colorectal surgery for benign or malignant disease

interventions.name: Control group: Patients undergo the established ERAS protocol without dedicated support from an ERAS nurse. Preoperatively, they receive only the ERAS information brochure containing the relevant recommendations and an ERAS diary for use during their hospital stay. No additional ward rounds or visit

Intervention group: Patients undergo the established ERAS protocol and, from the day of their outpatient clinic appointment and enrolment in the ERAS programme through surgery until hospital discharge, receive daily visits and support from an ERAS nurse. The ERAS nurse provides continuous guidance,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients undergoing elective colon or rectal surgery for benign or malignant disease
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Able to provide informed consent
- No previous participation in or education regarding an ERAS® programme
- Physically and cognitively able to participate in postoperative mobilisation (e.g. no pre-existing bedridden status or permanent wheelchair dependence)
- No contraindications to wearing an activity tracker
- No significant language barrier
Exclusion criteria:
- Declined participation in the ERAS® programme
- Requirement for postoperative intensive care beyond postoperative day 1 (POD 1)
- Abandonment of the planned surgical procedure
- Major postoperative complications (Clavien–Dindo Classification grade ≥ IIIb)
- Participation in other clinical studies that could influence the study outcomes
